mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the cases when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the cases when UNRATE increases by 0.2pp, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is strong but unemployment (UNRATE) is high, it indicates potential economic instability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the cases when GDPC1 and UNRATE indicate instability, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the cases when INDPRO increases by 1.0%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the cases when PAYEMS increases by 100,000, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A high consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) may lead to tighter monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the cases when CPIAUCSL is above 220, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the cases when HOUST increases by 10,000 units, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When real consumer spending (RSAFS) is high and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is low, it indicates strong demand and easy monetary conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the cases when RSAFS and FEDFUNDS indicate strong demand and low rates, this hypothesis is falsified.
